chapter_name: Care and Maintenance of Fabrics in Institutions
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the massive scale of commercial laundry systems and the science behind keeping fabrics clean and safe in hospitals and hotels!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Domestic laundry is done at home for a few people. Institutional laundry (in hospitals, hotels, prisons) handles hundreds of kilos of fabric daily, requiring industrial machinery, strict hygiene protocols, and specialized chemicals.

In hospitals, laundry must be completely disinfected to prevent infections. Soiled linens are categorized as infectious or non-infectious, and handled with extreme care using hot water and strong disinfectants.
For hotels, the focus is on aesthetics—crisp, white, and perfectly ironed bedsheets and towels to ensure guest satisfaction. This requires starches, optical brighteners, and heavy flatwork ironers.

The basic steps are: Collection, Sorting (by color, dirt level, infection risk), Washing (using large washer-extractors), Water Extraction, Drying (using tumblers), and Finishing/Ironing (using calenders).
Commercial laundries use more than just detergent. They use Alkalis (to remove heavy grease), Bleaches (to whiten and kill germs), Sours (acidic rinses to neutralize alkalis), and Fabric Softeners.

fun_activity.title: 🏷️ Care Label Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your closet and check the tags on three different items of clothing (e.g., a cotton t-shirt, a wool sweater, and a silk dress). Look at the laundry symbols. Which one says 'Dry Clean Only'? Which one allows bleaching?

exam_tips: 📌 Be ready to explain the difference in priorities between Hospital laundry (hygiene/disinfection) and Hotel laundry (aesthetics/crispness).
📌 Know what a 'Hydro-extractor' does: it spins fabrics at high speeds to remove excess water before drying.
📌 Memorize the standard sequence of the laundry process: Sort -> Wash -> Extract -> Dry -> Finish.
quick_recap: ⭐ Proper sorting prevents cross-contamination and fabric damage.
⭐ 'Calendering' is the industrial term for pressing flat linens like bedsheets using heated rollers.
⭐ Large institutions usually have their own in-house laundry departments to manage the massive daily volume.
